g1.label: 1. The numbers seem to ___ it
g1.why: The text says the numbers 'prove' that the USA is a nation of inventors.

g2.label: 2. More than 300,000 ___ every year
g2.why: The text says Americans register more than 300,000 patents every year.

g3.label: 3. The ___, the telephone and the aeroplane
g3.why: The text names the light bulb, the telephone and the aeroplane as US inventions.

g4.label: 4. Born in simple ___
g4.why: The text says many inventions were born in simple workshops.

g5.label: 5. Edison's laboratory ___ over 200 people
g5.why: The text says the Menlo Park laboratory employed over 200 people.

g6.label: 6. Turned it into a ___
g6.why: The text says a working idea was turned into a product for factories.

g7.label: 7. ___ will often give them millions
g7.why: The text says investors often give young programmers millions of dollars.

g8.label: 8. Encourage ___
g8.why: The text says schools should encourage creativity in the next generation.

g1.label: 1. If you ___ the museum
g1.why: Type 1: the if-clause takes the present simple, the main clause takes will + verb.

g2.label: 2. There ___ more female inventors
g2.why: Real possibility: the main clause of a type-1 conditional takes will + verb.

g3.label: 3. If you ___ this experiment
g3.why: After 'if' in type 1, use the present simple ('try'), not 'will'.

g4.label: 4. People ___ it
g4.why: The likely result goes in the main clause with 'will' + infinitive.

g5.label: 5. Electric cars ___ more popular
g5.why: Type 1 main clause: 'will become' for a likely future result.

g6.label: 6. If you ___ your project on time
g6.why: After 'if' in a type-1 sentence, use the present simple ('finish').

g7.label: 7. You ___ touch the machines
g7.why: Review from 8g-school-life-rules: 'mustn't' expresses a prohibition; the if-clause stays present simple.

g8.label: 8. You ___ that it is new
g8.why: Type 1: present simple in the if-clause ('prove'), 'will' in the main clause.

g1.label: 1. If I ___ an inventor
g1.why: Type 2 (imaginary): use 'were' for all persons in the if-clause.

g3.label: 3. If you ___ enough money
g3.why: Imaginary situation: past simple ('had') in the if-clause.

g4.label: 4. Travelling ___ much longer
g4.why: Unreal present: the main clause takes 'would' + infinitive.

g5.label: 5. If we ___ telephones
g5.why: Type 2 if-clause: past simple ('didn't have') for an imaginary present.

g6.label: 6. If I ___ to California
g6.why: Type 2: past simple ('travelled') after 'if' for an imagined action.

g7.label: 7. The world ___ working
g7.why: Imaginary future: the main clause takes 'would' + infinitive.

g8.label: 8. If it ___ real
g8.why: Type 2 uses 'were' (not 'is') for unreal situations in formal English.
